basis: Defining skin and eye defects; cardiomyopathy/arrhythmia and structural brain abnormalities/developmental delay each reported in 1/2 patients.
Immune-mediated inflammation of cutaneous small blood vessels defines the disease.
Inherited branched-chain amino acid metabolic disorders; neurological injury varies across subtypes and is not established across most of this umbrella.
Carcinoma originates in the thyroid endocrine gland; metastatic organ involvement is not universal.
Defective thyroid iodide uptake causes congenital hypothyroidism; permanent neurological injury is not intrinsic to every treated case.
Defined by disease of the eye, ocular adnexa or orbital region.
A depressive mood disorder; its psychiatric and vegetative symptoms do not establish damage to an organ axis.
Benign tumor of the tonsil in the pharynx, which belongs to the pulmonary axis; no immune mechanism is specified.
Defined here as Trichomonas vaginitis; reproductive tissue has no anatomical axis. Urinary tract involvement occurs in subtypes, without a common frequency established.
Clonal Langerhans-cell neoplasm; single-system multifocal disease most commonly involves multiple bones, supporting skeletal infiltration in >30%.
Congenital failure of normal osseous continuity and union in the radius.
Developmental delay, intellectual disability and infantile hypotonia define neurological involvement; borderline lactate alone does not establish metabolic disease.
Mesenchymal tumor arising in bone or soft tissue; associated tumor-induced osteomalacia is a separately diagnosed paraneoplastic metabolic syndrome.
Malignant epithelial tumor originates in the exocrine pancreas; jaundice alone does not establish direct hepatic damage.
Primary cerebral growth disorder with microcephaly and intellectual disability; hearing impairment is occasional (5–29%).
OCLN-related brain malformation with seizures and developmental impairment; patent ductus arteriosus in 2/5 (40%); ocular and renal findings are occasional.
Defining limb malformations; microcephaly is frequent (30–79%). Mullerian and external genital anomalies have no applicable axis.
Neoplastic or non-neoplastic polyp arising from the stomach.
Motor neuron degeneration defines ALS; muscle wasting is secondary to denervation. Associated frontotemporal dementia remains within the neurological axis.
GI abnormalities 80–99%; eye abnormalities including optic atrophy 30–79%. Liver, skeletal, hearing, respiratory and cardiac findings (30–79%) omitted at cap.
Pathological brain calcification with ataxia, parkinsonism and cognitive deterioration; no systemic mineral metabolism disorder is established.
Defining hyaline deposition causes skin nodules (34/35), gingival overgrowth (33/35), contractures and osteolysis. Recurrent infections alone do not prove immunodeficiency.
Malignant tumor of the parietal pleura; pleura belongs to the pulmonary axis.
Motor neuron degeneration defines ALS; respiratory insufficiency in 2/6 reflects denervated respiratory muscles rather than direct pulmonary disease.
Umbrella of congenital cortical malformations with lissencephaly; additional skeletal or systemic findings depend on subtype.
